why: Replaces Hermes's context engine with deterministic digests and byte-exact recall, a deep change with many tests; but it is a Claude Code/Codex proxy project thinly wrapped for Hermes: five-line manifest, six private core imports flagged by the catalog check, and savings that are modelled rather than measured. (Useful 4, Reliable 2, Polish 3, Creative 4, Beyond 5.)

Replaces Hermes's context engine with a deterministic one that stubs old tool results and lets the model recall them, so it works on every turn once installed; 498 tests passed here and catalog check, enable and doctor passed, but the check warns of private core imports (it wraps Hermes's own compressor), the savings figures are the author's own replays, and the README leads with a proxy for other agents.

U5/R4/P4/C4/B5: Deterministic context selection, cache-aware folding and byte-exact recall address a recurring cost of using Hermes itself and win this score tie on daily retention, but private compressor/pricing dependencies and less cohesive plugin-specific onboarding reduce confidence and polish; advertised savings were not independently reproduced (pinned source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeremiebergel/context-manager-intelligence/399468f0687c051476961e4bb045eb84263be6b1/README.md).

reads.worst: Normal setup depends on an external JustYou package and signed bindings, and the code supports reading bearer tokens and HMAC authority material from files outside Hermes’s secret store.

reads.best: A visible dashboard companion driven by real agent hooks, with screenshots and a clip browser site.

reads.best: Deterministic per-request verdicts, fixed loop goals, browser/network guards and real-browser test cases add useful evidence beyond asking a vision model to review a page.
